interpretation: Character-only already has two similar figures, four same-near-glove attempts and no vest. All six merged arms show one figure. Duplication, repetition and wardrobe omission therefore cannot all be blamed on merging; the flawed anchor is retained, not replaced with a more favorable seed.

Base/effect-only have two alternating attempts and a modest lower-chest final recovery, but no distinct subsequent lowering phase. Both depict a markedly different long-horned, angular/tusked/bearded design. Their action counts are not a combined identity/action success.

Additive makes four attempts (near-near-far-far), NP five (near-far-far-far-far), stable winner five same-far, TIES four same-far, SLERP three same-far and CT three (far-far-near). None reproduces exactly the requested two alternating punches with the full guard/ending sequence.

SLERP AND CT retain the vest in this seed; vest retention is not exclusive to CT. Both retain short-curved-horn green/purple cues with brow/muzzle/eye/teeth differences from creator/character-only. CT's more frontal pose and the anchor's two figures prevent a reliable fine-severity ranking against SLERP.

SLERP and TIES show a held final guard followed by clear lowering. Additive/NP retreat into lowering without a separately held full guard; CT has a brief lower-chest recovery then lowering; stable winner lowers only at the very end and remains in motion. Attempt count alone is not full prompt adherence.

NP has no demonstrated identity advantage over additive and adds a fifth clear extension in this cell. This negative cell prevents turning the earlier crossed-seed41 local NP ordering advantage into a universal recommendation.

Effect-only has four main waveform groups despite only two visual punches, with two groups during pauses. NP has five visible extensions but four broad energy groups. Neither energy grouping nor maxima is a valid action-count or perceived-sync surrogate.

interpretation: Every arm starts with a genuinely raised or partly open top cover, not the requested closed blue book. Character-only and all six merged arms do not establish a library; base/effect-only retain visible shelves. Initial book state and loss of setting are already present in the character-only control.

Character-only and all six merged arms retain coarse long-dark-haired facial cues, white blouse, full head and shoulder outline. Differences in hair drape, face angle, expression and light preclude a calibrated fine identity ordering. Base/effect-only differ in shoulder-length straight hair and narrower/longer facial presentation.

Additive and NP are especially close in matched views. Both open the already raised cover farther and end with a wedge/offset book alignment; SLERP has a similar object-state fault and less certain book-focused opening gaze. The already-contacting hand follows the cover downward rather than independently arriving later.

TIES, stable winner and CT close the book and show a later hovering/flattening hand placement after the smile. This is clearer than additive/NP in this cell, but none fixes the initially open book or missing library. Character-only itself has later finger flattening that is not independently separated from closure.

NP has no demonstrated improvement over additive in identity, library or book/hand sequence. CT has a local hand-placement/object-ending advantage over additive/NP, shared with stable winner and TIES, without a proven overall identity/style/AV advantage.
